title: Coherent two-sided bar from a bimodule and a left module
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $\mathcal V$ be a monoidal infinity-category and $\mathcal M$ an infinity-category with a coherent left action $\otimes:\mathcal V\times\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$: the equivalences $(v\otimes w)\otimes m\simeq v\otimes(w\otimes m)$ and $\mathbf1\otimes m\simeq m$ include all associative and unital higher compatibilities. An associative algebra $B$ in $\mathcal V$ has a multiplication $B\otimes B\to B$, a unit $\mathbf1\to B$ and their coherent compatibilities. A left $B$-module in $\mathcal M$ has an action $B\otimes m\to m$ with all coherent associativity and unit data; $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ retains the coherent action-preserving maps and their higher simplices. For each associative algebra $D$ in $\mathcal V$, write $U_D:\operatorname{LMod}_D(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal M$ for the functor forgetting the module structure. All categories and mapping spaces are taken in sufficiently large universes. Let $A,B$ be associative algebras in $\mathcal V$. Let $P\in\mathcal V$ have a coherent left $B$-action and right $A$-action, unital, associative and commuting with all higher compatibilities (a $(B,A)$-bimodule), and let $Q\in\operatorname{LMod}_A(\mathcal M)$. There is a coherent simplicial diagram
$$\operatorname{Bar}_A(P,Q):N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M),\qquad [n]\longmapsto P\otimes A^{\otimes n}\otimes U_AQ,$$
where $\Delta$ is the category of finite nonempty ordered sets and monotone maps, and the $B$-action is through $P$. For $n\geq1$, $d_0$ uses the right action on $P$, $d_i$ for $0<i<n$ multiplies the $i$th and $(i+1)$st $A$ factors, and $d_n$ uses the action on $Q$. For $0\leq i\leq n$, $s_i$ inserts the unit of $A$ between the $i$th and $(i+1)$st positions in the ordered word, whose endpoints are $P$ and $Q$. All parenthesizations are related by the specified coherent tensor and action equivalences. These data define the entire coherent diagram, naturally in $P,Q$ and their coherent module maps, without assuming any colimits.

More generally an augmentation to $N\in\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ is induced by a $B$-linear coherently $A$-balanced pairing $P\otimes U_AQ\to U_BN$: balanced means equipped with the compatibility between the right $A$-action on $P$ and the left $A$-action on $Q$, including all higher compatibilities. Its degree-$n$ map is the pairing after applying the intervening $A$ factors by these actions. The diagram is compatible with coherent ordered-tensor-word evaluation: consecutive blocks are contracted by multiplication or endpoint actions, empty blocks insert units, and strings of contractions use the specified operadic substitution coherences. This evaluation is compatible with adding or removing unit blocks.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Construction 4.4.2.7, printed p. 576, with the action-valued variant of Examples 4.4.2.11-12; ordered-word description from Construction 4.2.2.6 and Example 4.7.2.7. Only construction of the simplicial object is asserted, not the relative tensor-product colimit theorem 4.4.2.8. Online 2017 source read; WANTED: archived Higher Algebra in literature/. No Stacks tag covers coherent infinity-categorical modules.

proof.text: Write $\mathsf{BM}$ for the planar operad with colours $v,m,t$ and its unique operations $v^r\to v$, $t^s\to t$, and $v^rmt^s\to m$, for $r,s\geq0$. The coherent left action gives a coherent functor on its operator category: the colour fibers are $\mathcal V,\mathcal M,*$, the fiber at a list is the product of its colour fibers, and a block operation acts by the given iterated tensor/action, with the terminal right factors ignored. The functoriality simplices are the assumed tensor/action associativity and unit coherences, including the higher ones. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], in an enlarged universe containing these categories, to obtain $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{BM}^\otimes)$. Its cocartesian transports are precisely these block tensor/action functors. For an operator $\alpha$ and tuples $x,y$ over its source and target, take a cocartesian edge $x\to\alpha_!x$. The cocartesian mapping-space pullback square in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], restricted to the fiber over $\alpha$ and the identity of its target, identifies maps from $x$ to $y$ over $\alpha$ with maps $\alpha_!x\to y$ in the target fiber. This fiber is a product, so that mapping space is the product of the mapping spaces from the individual transported blocks to the corresponding components of $y$. Thus the product decomposition on lists and the relative mapping-space product decomposition of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] make $\mathcal E^\otimes$ an operadic target: inert transports are the coordinate projections. This constructs the action-valued cocartesian fibration from the given coherent action, without asking for any colimit.

source.place: Example 4.4.2.12, the bitensored setting with terminal right monoidal category; Construction 4.4.2.7, its cocartesian-fibration hypothesis.

proof.text: Use $\mathsf{Chain}_2$ of [lem-coef-composable-bimodule-operad-segal]. Map its colours $a_0,a_1,p$ to $v$, its colour $q$ to $m$, and its colour $a_2$ to $t$. This gives a map $g$ of operator categories into $\mathsf{BM}^\otimes$: every allowed block has the required output type. On $\mathsf{BM}_{01}$ the given $(B,A)$-bimodule $P$ defines an algebra lift with values $(B,P,A)$; on $\mathsf{BM}_{12}$ the left $A$-module $Q$ defines a lift with values $(A,Q,*)$, where the right terminal action is the identity. Their restrictions to $a_1$ are the same specified algebra $A$. The relative restriction equivalence in the cited node therefore packages them as an inert-preserving coherent functor $F_0:N(\mathsf{Chain}_2^\otimes)\to\mathcal E^\otimes$ equipped with a coherent equivalence $qF_0\simeq g$. This is an equivalence of full infinity-categories of input structures, so retains their coherent maps and all parameter simplices. No tensor product over $A$ has been formed.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.1.11 and Remark 4.4.2.2, relative version; Example 4.4.2.12, terminal right action.

proof.text: Define $w:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Chain}_2^\otimes$ by $w[n]=(p,a_1,\ldots,a_1,q)$ with $n$ middle colours. For $f:[m]\to[n]$, its contravariant arrow contracts $p,a_{1,1},\ldots,a_{1,f(0)}$ to $p$; for $1\leq j\leq m$ it contracts the block numbered $f(j-1)+1,\ldots,f(j)$ to the $j$th output $a_1$; and it contracts the remaining middle colours together with $q$ to $q$. An empty middle block uses the nullary $a_1$ operation. Equivalently the underlying interval map sends $0\mapsto0$, $j+1\mapsto f(j)+1$ for $0\leq j\leq m$, and $m+2\mapsto n+2$. This preserves both outer endpoints. Refining these consecutive blocks for a second monotone map gives exactly the blocks for the composite, and $\mathsf{Chain}_2$ has just one operation of each allowed type; hence this is an ordinary functor, including identities. Its base map $gw$ has a natural transformation $\beta$ to the constant one-letter word $m$: at each word use the single operation contracting all $v$ factors and the final $m$. Naturality holds because both composite block substitutions are that same unique operation of $\mathsf{BM}$.

source.place: Notation 4.4.2.4 and Construction 4.4.2.7; explicit planar cut-word formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $q$, $K=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, $F_0w$, and the transformation $\gamma:qF_0w\to\operatorname{const}(m)$ obtained by composing the specified equivalence $qF_0w\simeq gw$ with $\beta$. Thus an infinity-categorical lift from step 2 suffices; no identification of a strict fiber with a homotopy fiber is required. The index category is countable and thus small; the source and target of $q$ are quasicategories, and its cocartesian lifts exist by step 1 with the mapping-space characterization stated in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. We get a coherent diagram $X_\bullet$ in the fiber $\mathcal E_m=\mathcal M$. Its degree $n$ is the transport of $(P,A,\ldots,A,U_AQ)$ along the total contraction, namely $P\otimes A^{\otimes n}\otimes U_AQ$. The same transport theorem says that transport of a substituted sequence agrees coherently with its composite. Therefore the maps of $X$ are the word contractions and unit insertions of step 3, with their entire strings of substitution simplices; this constructs the whole coherent simplicial diagram, rather than just its edges and pairwise identities.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7: lift the transformation to the constant output colour by cocartesian transport; no use of Theorem 4.4.2.8.

proof.text: Perform this transport simultaneously on the subcategory of $\mathsf{Chain}_2^\otimes$ whose words are $a_0^r p a_1^n q$, for $r,n\geq0$, and whose arrows use the allowed block operations over interval maps preserving both outer endpoints, while retaining one $p$ and one $q$. Thus no input is discarded, and the total contractions again form a natural transformation to the constant colour $m$. Restriction to $r=0$ is step 4. Its total tensor at $(r,n)$ is coherently $B^{\otimes r}\otimes X_n$, because successive tensor transports compose as in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. The block $a_0^r p\to p$ gives its action to $X_n$; substitution of $a_0$ multiplication and nullary operations gives the associative and unital $B$-module coherences in every dimension. In the joint word category, applying an $a_0$ block and an $a_1$ block in either order has the same substitution. The full coherent $F_0$ therefore supplies the action-preserving simplices for every $n$-map and for every string of them. By the meaning of $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ in the statement, this is a coherent simplicial diagram in that category, with left action through $P$. For the coface omitting $0$, the initial block is $p,a_1$; omitting an interior vertex joins its two adjacent $a_1$ factors; omitting $n$ gives the last block $a_1,q$. Repeating a vertex produces an empty middle block. These are exactly $d_0,d_i,d_n,s_i$ with the asserted indices, including $s_0:P\otimes Q\to P\otimes A\otimes Q$ in degree zero.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7; retention of the external algebra action, and Example 4.4.2.12. Explicit degree-zero and generator calculation.

proof.text: Let $b:P\otimes U_AQ\to U_BN$ be the specified balanced, $B$-linear pairing. On a word $a_0^r p a_1^n q$, first apply the iterated left $A$-action to the final $Q$, then apply $b$, and then the $r$-fold $B$-action on $N$. These operations give a coherent transformation from the pre-transport word diagram to the constant object $N$ over total contraction. To check its content, an interior $a_1$ contraction or an empty $a_1$ block is compatible by the associativity or unit data of the $A$-action; the terminal block is compatible by the same iterated action. An initial $p,a_1$ contraction moves that $A$ factor through $b$, and the required comparison is exactly the supplied balancing homotopy. A prefix $a_0$ contraction uses exactly the supplied $B$-linearity. For an arbitrary string of block contractions these are the specified higher balancing and linearity compatibilities, evaluated on the corresponding nested blocks; they are part of the coherent pairing hypothesis, not inferred from pairwise equalities. Apply the mapping-space fiber equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to this transformation. It factors coherently through the transported word diagram and hence gives a cocone $X_\bullet\to N$. Since the prefix words were included, it is a cocone in $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$. Its degree-zero map is $b$ and its degree-$n$ map is the pairing after the intervening $A$-actions, as claimed.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7 with a specified balanced output pairing; factorization through the cocartesian total-tensor edges.

proof.text: The equivalence in [lem-coef-composable-bimodule-operad-segal] is an equivalence of infinity-categories of input structures, including their coherent maps. Represent a parameter simplex by its family over a small simplicial set $T$, and apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] once with index $T\times N(\mathsf{Pre})$, where $\mathsf{Pre}$ is the prefix-word category of step 5. Its constant-output fiber is $\operatorname{Fun}(T\times N(\mathsf{Pre}),\mathcal M)$. Restricting this lifted transformation to any face, degeneracy or vertex of $T$ again has cocartesian vertex components, so is the transport of that restricted input family by the pointwise criterion. Restricting further to zero-prefix words gives the asserted family of bars. The same restriction of the mapping-space factorization in step 6 gives its family of augmentations. Thus the construction retains every input-map simplex and is natural in $P,Q$ and the specified balanced pairing.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7, applied to parameterized input families; restriction of a coherent diagram and the pointwise criterion.

proof.text: For two consecutive word substitutions, apply the composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]: successive transports agree coherently with transport along their composite, compatibly with the precomposition maps used in step 6. Repeating this clause for a finite string gives the same specified coherent comparisons. Staged parenthesizations are these successive transports, so this supplies the asserted compatibility with total ordered-word contraction.

source.place: Construction 4.4.2.7; direct specialization of coherent transport composition.

proof.text: In the operator category of [lem-coef-composable-bimodule-operad-segal], an empty algebra block is its nullary operation. Inserting it and then contracting it with a neighbouring block substitutes that nullary operation into the multiplication or module action, yielding the original operation: the permitted operation set is a singleton and substitution is unital. Apply the coherent functor $F_0$ to this equality and to strings containing it. The composition comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies evaluation by those substitutions with evaluation by total contraction. Hence adding and removing unit blocks gives the asserted unit comparison with all further substitution coherences.

source.place: Constructions 4.2.2.6 and 4.4.2.7; nullary operations, operadic substitution, and transport composition.

proof.text: In the specialization $B=A$, $P=A$ with both actions multiplication, the regular lift constructed in step 2 satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-coef-two-sided-bar-leading-unit-extension]. That node evaluates the restricted word $a_1^kq$ as $A^{\otimes k}\otimes U_AQ$ and evaluates the opposite interval map $h(0)=h(1)=0$, $h(j)=j-1$ for $j\ge2$, as $\eta_A\otimes\operatorname{id}$ in $\mathcal M$ after forgetting the external action.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Construction 4.4.2.7 and action-valued Example 4.4.2.12, regular leading-unit specialization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-two-sided-bar-regular-word-identification] to the same regular lift: the regular bimodule $P=A$ of step 2 is the algebra $A$ restricted along $\mathsf{BM}_{01}\to\mathsf{Ass}_1$ (all three colours to $a_1$), which is that node's hypothesis. Relabelling $p$ as the first $a_1$ gives the functor $r:R\to W$, and its evaluated comparison identifies the regular bar diagram $Y$ with $X\circ N(r)$, coherently for all strings in $R$. The larger diagram $X$ also evaluates strings in $W$ containing a leading-unit insertion, as in step 10. Thus $X$ extends the regular bar evaluation to those strings. This comparison takes place in $\mathcal M$ after forgetting the external left action; it does not assert that a leading insertion lies in the image of $r$ or is $A$-linear.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Construction 4.4.2.7 and Example 4.4.2.12, regular-word identification.

proof_origin.place: Source-guided expansion of HA Proposition 4.4.1.11, Notation 4.4.2.4 and Construction 4.4.2.7, with the action model of Example 4.4.2.12. Source read online; no archived copy in literature/.
